Team —

Quick weekly flashline on wins / risks / asks as we lock the QBR pack. This is targeted at the exec distribution for visibility; please flag anything you want pulled into the QBR highlights by EOD. Attach: compact QBR draft + latency heatmap (key chart).

Wins
- Redwood Dedicated pilot with Northstar finished validation on Wednesday; 2 customers (Acme POC) saw 18% lower p50 latency with our batching tweaks. Baseline metrics in attached PDF.
- Initial Optimize pilot suggestions (quantization + prefix caching) delivered projected 12% token-cost savings for mid-size workloads.
- CS successfully closed uplift renewal for BetaRetail; churn risk reduced to low.

Risks / Open Issues
- Capacity commit for Dedicated in EU region: procurement redline pending legal signoff and could slip into next quarter (impact = delayed SLA offering for two enterprise prospects).
- Latency variance: onboarding load tests show a 95th-percentile spike on long-context (>8k) runs; root cause points to current kernel fallback under memory pressure. Need a rollout plan for kernel tweaks.
- QBR narrative: we need tighter revenue/ARR impact from Optimize recommendations; finance needs a conservative estimate for the deck.

Asks / Requests
- @Jonas: please confirm whether we can exempt the EU procurement item from the standard RFP timeline; need yes/no by EOD.
- @Laura: add a one-line ask on capacity commitment in the QBR slides if legal cannot expedite.
- @Marissa: include top two customer quotes (BetaRetail + Acme) in the customer impact slide; I left a placeholder.
- @Vivek: agree on go/no-go for kernel rollout (low-risk canary vs full push).

Timeline and next steps
- Today: internal reviews and slide polishing.
- Wed 12/2: dry run with execs (10:00 PT).
- Fri 12/4: finalize QBR deck to board package.

Attachments: QBR-draft-compact.pdf, latency-heatmap.png
Drive draft: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBRdraftRk

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
